key_insight: The paper proposes a fidelity-style accuracy metric for quantum annealing that evaluates the quality of the annealing process itself, not just whether the optimization problem is solved.
engineering_relevance: This gives hardware teams a problem-independent benchmark for comparing annealers against classical thermal behavior and for setting concrete precision targets for future quantum annealing devices.
method: Define an annealing fidelity metric as an accuracy ε for the annealer’s equation of state.
Benchmark ε using variational quantum Monte Carlo with a thermal-annealing-inspired ansatz on Rydberg atom systems.
Cross-check with Green function quantum Monte Carlo to reach higher-precision reference values.
evidence_signal: The simulations report ε≈10^-2 to 10^-3 up to 100,000,000 atoms with variational QMC and ε≈10^-4 up to 100,000 atoms with Green function QMC, exceeding current experimental platforms by orders of magnitude.
watch_item: The metric is benchmarked on Rydberg-atom simulation models, so transferring the same precision claims to other hardware platforms or problem classes may require additional validation.
paper_title: A fidelity metric for quantum annealing benchmarked by extreme scaling quantum Monte-Carlo simulations
